label: Aristotle, Physics VIII.5, 256a13-21: It is impossible that there be no mover that is not…
interpretation: If everything moved is moved by something, either by a thing moved by another or not, there must be a mover not moved by another (ἀνάγκη τι εἶναι κινοῦν ὃ οὐχ ὑπʼ ἄλλου πρῶτον). Stated as a reductio, as the prima via's conclusion is. It is weaker than the prima via's 'moved by none': Aristotle goes on (256a19-21) to say that such a first mover, if moved, moves itself; that further step is not formalized here. Scope: Aristotle's physical motion; the Lean has no guard, so the reading is accepted only under a physical instantiation of `MovedIn`/`MovesIn` (DISAMB-MOTION). 'First' (πρῶτον) is not formalized: the mover is not shown to head any particular series.
